Round 2 · Implementation · Hard

Ticket #17 — Background Job Queue

Difficulty: Hard

Context

You maintain background work such as digest emails and image resizing. A lease gives one worker temporary ownership of a job. Another worker may reclaim the job after that lease expires if the attempt limit allows it. now is a supplied numeric time; no real waiting is needed in tests.

Practice report

Enqueue job-1, then call claim("worker-a", 100) with a 30-second lease and maximum 3 attempts. Immediately call claim("worker-b", 100).

Observation after the second claim Current starter Expected
Returned job job-1 None
Stored lease owner worker-b worker-a
Attempt count 2 1

These are sequential calls at the same supplied time; the report requires no thread scheduler to reproduce.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A live lease excludes other workers. Each successful claim records one owner, increments attempts once, and sets a deadline using the configured lease duration.
  • At the exact deadline the lease is expired. An eligible expired job can be reclaimed without losing attempt history.
  • Only the current owner of an unexpired lease can complete or fail it. A stale worker or wrong worker gets conflict without changing the current lease.
  • Completion makes a job done; repeated completion is harmless and a done job is never claimed again.
  • A reported failure records the error and requeues the job until the attempt limit; the final failure is terminal. If the final worker disappears, the next claim after expiry marks the exhausted job failed without reclaiming it.
  • Duplicate job IDs are rejected without replacement. Missing completion and invalid ownership requests follow the existing result contract without new jobs.

Out of Scope

Keep the supplied job store, payloads, and timestamp API. Running the actual job, database locking, distributed worker coordination, and new configuration validation are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Trace claim, completion, failure, and reclaim through stored owner, status, attempt count, and deadline. Add deterministic tests before and at expiry, a stale worker after reassignment, a reported retry, and a vanished final worker. Explain which state proves that only one lease is live.
